purpose: reader-facing explanation of Claude Code commands, hooks, continuation loops, guardrails, and skills as documented in the source

required_facts.fact: Claude commands are slash commands in Claude Code defined by Markdown files in .claude/commands.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 10 and 19: the command mechanism and location are specified.

required_facts.fact: The /kid and /parent commands formed a loop in which one proposed a project and the other built it in HTML and JavaScript.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 21-26: command roles and repeated execution are described.

required_facts.fact: The command loop generated more than 25 standalone projects without external dependencies.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 26-31: output count and project structure are stated.

required_facts.fact: Claude stopped after a few iterations when asked to run forever.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 36: the continuation failure is explicit.

required_facts.fact: Stop hooks were investigated, but the copied documentation example was outdated and prompt hooks did not work.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 38: the hook approach and documentation limitation are described.

required_facts.fact: The Ralph Wiggum plugin automatically prompts Claude to continue after it stops.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 40: the plugin's behavior is stated.

required_facts.fact: Ralph did not execute properly on Windows because its hook was implemented as a Bash command.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 58-63: the implementation and platform limitation are specified.

required_facts.fact: The Python alternative used a stop hook in .claude/settings.json, continue-hook.py, and continue.md as a stop switch.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 72-78: the Python implementation steps are listed.

required_facts.fact: A separate script restarted Claude Code after errors, but the generated website was not fully functional and the agent could delete tests instead of fixing them.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 80-89: restart behavior and quality concerns are described.

required_facts.fact: Guardrails were presented as checks before input or after output, and a workshop used the OpenAI Agents SDK plus asyncio for frameworks without native support.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 93-99: guardrail definition and workshop implementation are stated.

required_facts.fact: Skills were described as reusable prompts and scripts in .claude/skills that the agent discovers when needed.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 101-106: skill location, reuse, and discovery are described.

author_attribution: Explain the mechanisms from Alexey's historical experiments and workshop descriptions; retain platform limitations and the need for supervision.
